properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (the field-feedback rule). From bhome S3: the plan-sheet generator cites the IFC mechanically and cites the graph through design-facts.json, a hand copy of budget_report, so 'the half of the sheet reflow2 owns is the half with no mechanical guarantee'. OPTIONS, none chosen: (a) a one-shot CLI door — `reflow2-mcp --graph-path … --call budget_report '{"constraint_id":…}'` printing the tool's JSON and exiting — the smallest change, the same binary, no agent, respects the single-writer lock the way --export-snapshot does; (b) derived views written through like the export: name a report and a path and the server keeps the file current after every change (the docs-as-views direction, dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph, turned into a mechanism instead of an agent act); (c) document tools/smoke_mcp.py's stdio client as the consumer door — it exists and drives every gate here; (d) leave it: the sheet says in terms that it cannot see the budget move. COUNTER to (b): a report is computed and can be large; a file per report per change is the auto-export cost times the number of views; (a) puts the cadence in the build, where the reporter already has one.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a build script read a budget (or any report) from the graph without an agent and without a hand transcription — a one-shot CLI call, a report the server writes through like the export, or a documented stdio client?
properties.rationale: Recorded from the field report beside the docs-as-views idea rather than folded into it: that one asks whether the AGENT renders documents from graph data; this asks for a door a BUILD can use with no agent in the loop.
